item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Which angle in the figure has a measure closest to 45°?

[Image: Circle divided into angles p, q, r, and s]
item.figure_description: A circle contains a vertical diameter dividing it into left and right halves. From the center, two additional line segments (radii) are drawn: one extending to the left edge at roughly 9 o'clock (slightly below horizontal), and another extending down and to the right at approximately a 45-degree angle from the vertical. Four central angles are labeled: angle q is in the upper-left quadrant (between the upward vertical radius and the left radius, roughly 90°); angle p is in the lower-left quadrant (between the left radius and the downward vertical radius, roughly 90°); angle r is in the upper-right (between the upward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, an obtuse angle of roughly 135°); and angle s is in the lower-right (between the downward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, roughly 45°).
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Geometric construction with intersecting arcs]

In the figure above, an arc of a circle with center P has been drawn to cut the line at Q. Then an arc with the same radius and center Q was drawn to cut the first arc at R. What would be the size of angle PRQ?
reference_items.figure_description: A horizontal straight line has two marked points, P to the left and Q to the right. An arc of a circle centered at point P begins at point Q on the line and curves up and to the left. A second, shorter arc centered at point Q intersects the first arc at a marked point labeled R, which lies above the line segment PQ.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
What fraction of the circle is shaded?

[Image: A circle divided into two sectors, one shaded and one unshaded]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle with a center dot. Two radii divide the circle into two sectors. One radius extends straight up from the center to the 12 o'clock position. The other radius extends to the left, slightly below the horizontal 9 o'clock position. The larger sector, which runs clockwise from the top radius around through the right side and bottom to the lower-left radius, is shaded solid gray. The smaller remaining sector in the upper-left area is white (unshaded).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Coordinate grid with points P, Q, R, and S]

Which of the following represents the point (3, −2) on the graph?
reference_items.figure_description:
A Cartesian coordinate plane with horizontal axis x and vertical axis y intersecting at origin O. Each axis has three tick marks in each direction from the origin representing unit increments of 1, 2, 3 and -1, -2, -3. Four points are plotted:
- Point P is at coordinates (3, 2).
- Point Q is at coordinates (3, -2).
- Point R is at coordinates (-3, -2).
- Point S is at coordinates (-3, 2).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Triangle ABC]

What is the measure of angle C in the triangle above?
reference_items.figure_description: A right triangle ABC with the right angle at vertex A in the lower left, marked with a square symbol. The vertical side AB goes up to vertex B at the top, where the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 35°. The horizontal side AC extends to the right to vertex C, where an arc marks the interior angle.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which point on the graph could have coordinates (7,16)?

[Image: Coordinate grid with points P, Q, R, S]
reference_items.figure_description:
A first-quadrant Cartesian grid with a horizontal x-axis labeled with an arrow and 'x' at the right, and a vertical y-axis labeled with an arrow and 'y' at the top. The origin is labeled 0. Both axes have grid lines at intervals of 5, labeled 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. Four points are plotted on the grid:
- Point P: plotted at approximately x = 7, y = 6 (labeled '. P')
- Point Q: plotted at approximately x = 16, y = 6 (labeled '. Q')
- Point R: plotted at approximately x = 16, y = 16 (labeled '. R')
- Point S: plotted at approximately x = 7, y = 16 (labeled '. S')
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Regular hexagon PQRSTU]

PQRSTU is a regular hexagon. What is the measure of the angle QUS?
reference_items.figure_description: A regular hexagon with vertices labeled clockwise: P at the top left, Q at the top right, R at the far right, S at the bottom right, T at the bottom left, and U at the far left. Segment PQ forms the top horizontal edge, and segment TS forms the bottom horizontal edge. Two internal straight line segments are drawn: one connecting vertex U to vertex Q, and another connecting vertex U to vertex S, forming angle QUS.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle divided into 12 squares with some squares shaded]

Which circle has approximately the same fraction of its area shaded as the rectangle above?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a rectangle is divided into a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns, forming 12 equal-sized squares. The bottom row has all 4 squares shaded gray. The middle row has the leftmost square shaded gray and the other 3 squares unshaded (white). The top row has all 4 squares unshaded. In total, 5 of the 12 squares are shaded.

Each option shows a circle with a center point and radial lines dividing it into sectors, with one sector shaded gray:
- Option A: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and slightly left (about 6:30). The larger sector on the right side is shaded gray (covering slightly more than half of the circle).
- Option B: The circle is divided by a vertical diameter passing through the center from 12 o'clock to 6 o'clock. The right half of the circle is shaded gray (exactly 1/2 of the circle).
- Option C: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and a horizontal radius pointing left (9 o'clock). The sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock is shaded gray (3/4 of the circle).
- Option D: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and to the right (about 4:30 to 5 o'clock). The sector between them on the right side is shaded gray (covering somewhat less than half of the circle, approximately 5/12 of the area).
- Option E: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing up and slightly left (about 11 o'clock). The major sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 11 o'clock is shaded gray (covering almost the entire circle, about 11/12 of the area).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

In this figure PQ is a straight line.

[Image: Angles on a straight line]

What is the degree measure of angle PRS?

A ray labeled with endpoint S extends upward and to the left from R. The angle PRS is marked with an arc and labeled "2x". The adjacent angle SRQ is marked with an arc and labeled "7x".

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle ABCD containing two tangent circles P and Q]

In the figure above, ABCD is a rectangle, and circles P and Q each have a radius of 5 cm. What is the area of the rectangle?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle ABCD is oriented horizontally with vertices labeled A at the top-left, B at the top-right, C at the bottom-right, and D at the bottom-left. Inside the rectangle are two identical circles labeled P and Q, with their centers marked by dots labeled P and Q. The two circles are tangent to each other horizontally at the midline of the rectangle. Circle P touches the left side AD, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. Circle Q touches circle P, the right side BC, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. A vertical line segment is drawn from center P up to the point of tangency on top side AB, labeled "5 cm".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
